answer: Off the ridge coast, where the horizon meets the sea, pearl divers work from a single diving bell. Each diver owns one bell, lowered by a surface tender who logs depth and minutes down, while the diver gathers pearls by hand along the reef. Back on deck the tender weighs the catch in a dated pouch, the guild weigher stamps it, and a second tender signs the log before the dive counts. A diver caught filing two pouches from one dive forfeits the season's catch. A thousand fake names need a thousand bells, a thousand tenders, and a thousand stamped dives.
